title: The supposition: God's middle knowledge
source_text: CXXVII. Supponunt igitur authores istius sententiae Deum ab aeterno praescire per scientiam quam Scholae mediam, seu conditionatam vocant, quid hic aut ille homo facturus sit, si vocetur hoc aut illo modo, & si ad ipsum convertendum tales illustrationes & inspirationes, aliaque hujusmodi media, tum externa tum interna adhibeantur. Et quidem si hoc modo vocetur Petrus, verbi causa, illum secuturum, minime vero, si alio modo. Licet sive hoc sive illo modo vocetur, possit si velit sequi, vel non sequi.
pass_a_gloss: CXXVII. The authors of this opinion therefore suppose that God foreknows from eternity by the knowledge which the Schools call middle, or conditional, what this or that man will do, if he be called in this or that way, & if for converting him such illuminations & inspirations, and other means of this kind, both external and internal be applied. And indeed that if Peter, for example, be called in this way, he will follow, but not at all, if in another way. Although whether he be called in this or in that way, he can if he will follow, or not follow.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXXVII. The authors of this view therefore assume that God foreknows from eternity, by what the Schools call middle or conditional knowledge, what this or that person would do if he were called in one way or another, and if such illuminations and inspirations and other means, outward and inward, were used to convert him. If Peter, say, is called in this way, God knows he will follow; if in that way, not at all. Yet whichever way he is called, he can follow or not follow, as he wills.
